title: Reliability and Journalling in File Systems

blocks.text: Imagine your computer crashes while saving an important document. How does the file system ensure your data isn't lost or corrupted?

blocks.markdown: In this lesson, we will explore how file systems maintain reliability, particularly focusing on crash consistency and journalling. We'll also discuss the trade-offs between write caching and durability.

blocks.title: Crash Consistency
blocks.text: Crash consistency refers to the ability of a file system to maintain a consistent state even after a system crash during write operations.

blocks.markdown: When a system crash occurs during a write operation, the file system can be left in an inconsistent state. This inconsistency arises because write operations are often not atomic; they can be interrupted, leaving some parts of the file system updated while others are not.

blocks.latex: Consistency = \text{All operations are atomic and durable}
blocks.caption: Formal definition of consistency in file systems.

blocks.title: Example of Crash-Induced Inconsistency
blocks.prompt: Consider a file system where a file is being updated. The update involves writing to two separate blocks. A crash occurs after the first block is written but before the second block is updated.

steps.text: Step 1: The file system starts updating Block A and Block B.
Step 2: Block A is successfully written to the disk.
Step 3: A crash occurs before Block B is written.
Result: Block A is updated, but Block B is not, leading to an inconsistent state.

blocks.answer: The file system is left in an inconsistent state because only part of the update was completed.

blocks.markdown: To address this issue, file systems use journalling. Journalling ensures that all operations are recorded in a log before they are applied to the file system. This log can be used to restore consistency after a crash.

blocks.title: Journalling
blocks.text: Journalling is a technique where changes are first written to a log (journal) before being applied to the file system. This allows the system to recover to a consistent state after a crash.

blocks.title: Journalling in Action
blocks.prompt: Consider the same scenario as before, but now with a journalling file system.

steps.text: Step 1: The update operation is recorded in the journal.
Step 2: Block A is written to the disk.
Step 3: A crash occurs before Block B is written.
Step 4: Upon recovery, the system reads the journal and completes the update to Block B.

blocks.answer: The file system uses the journal to complete the update, restoring consistency.

blocks.markdown: While journalling improves reliability, it introduces a trade-off between write performance and durability. Write caching can improve performance but may compromise durability if a crash occurs before cached writes are committed to disk.

blocks.title: Trade-off: Write Caching vs. Durability
blocks.text: Write caching improves performance by delaying writes to disk, but it risks data loss during a crash. Journalling mitigates this risk by ensuring changes are logged before being applied.

points: Crash consistency is crucial for maintaining a reliable file system.
Journalling helps restore consistency after a crash by using a log.
There is a trade-off between write caching performance and data durability.
